summary: The listening tools are in tools/audio/listen: common.py (loading, resampling, output, device, GPU lock), measure.py (levels, BS.1770 loudness, spectrum, envelope, loop seam, spectrogram PNG), compare.py (CLAP, single and batch mode), transcribe.py (Whisper plus WER), describe.py (Qwen2-Audio-7B, runs here with bitsandbytes 4-bit). 22 unittest tests pass, none skipped. README.md, MODELS.md and requirements.txt are written.
verified: python -m unittest discover -s tools/audio/listen/tests -v: Ran 22 tests, OK, 0 skipped (CLAP and Whisper tests ran: English voice Microsoft Zira found for System.Speech).

measure.py on 3 real renders (alarm_heat, alarm_missile, cabin_ambience_loop) with --loop --png: output read; the cabin loop passes the seam check, the one-shot alarms report FAIL as expected for non-loops.

Spectrogram PNG alarm_heat.png opened with Read: waveform strip with a pulsing envelope, 864 Hz fundamental with horizontal harmonic lines at about 1.75 kHz and 2.6 kHz, a hard cutoff near 3 kHz, noise floor around -55 to -65 dB, and brief broadband spikes up to 20 kHz at the pulse onsets (0.25, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 1.75 s), which are clicks in the placeholder alarm.

compare.py single mode on a 1 kHz sine (pos beat 0.41 vs neg 0.12) and batch mode with --spec/--dir/--only on 3 real renders (writes assets/audio/cache/compare.json); all three placeholder sounds scored FAIL (a cheap electronic beep wins).
transcribe.py on synthesised speech: first run with the German default voice gave WER 0.222; the unit test with the English voice passes at WER <= 0.2.

describe.py with --mode bnb4 on a synthesised sentence, a sine and two real renders: it answered correctly for speech and sine, and said 'Siamese cat meowing' for alarm_heat and 'telephone dial tone' for cabin_ambience_loop. Load 12.3 to 15.5 s, GPU peak 6.35 to 6.45 GiB, 2.3 s for the first answer and 0.4 s for the next.
Measured model memory: CLAP 0.79 GiB GPU peak, Whisper fp16 0.56 GiB.
GPU lock: acquired and released in a direct test; no lock file remained after the tests. No servers or background processes were started.
notVerified: Licences of laion/larger_clap_general and openai/whisper-small could not be read from the cache (no README or licence file in the snapshots); MODELS.md records them as NOT VERIFIED with the upstream licence only from memory. The Qwen2-Audio licence (Apache-2.0) was read from its cached README.
describe.py --mode quanto and --mode offload were never run (bnb4 worked first); they are in the code as untested fallbacks.
Process RSS of describe.py was not measured; time of a cold first load of Qwen from disk was not measured (the cache was warm).
The GPU lock under real contention (two processes waiting, ten minute timeout, takeover of a dead owner) was not tested, only the uncontended path.
measure.py was only tried on mono and stereo 48 kHz and one 22.05 kHz file; no 24-bit or very long file was tried.
Loop swing and spectral edge difference are reported but have no hard threshold; only seamRatio (above 2 fails) and edge level difference (above 3 dB fails) decide loop.pass.
deviations: Installed from PyPI into .venv-audio: pyloudnorm 0.2.0, accelerate 1.15.0 (brought psutil 7.2.2), bitsandbytes 0.50.2. optimum-quanto, sentencepiece, protobuf were not installed.
LUFS uses pyloudnorm rather than an own implementation; clips under 400 ms are repeated to one block (noted in the output).
The model tools (compare, transcribe, describe, and the model tests) all take the GPU lock, not only describe, so a small model cannot run out of memory next to the 4-bit Qwen.
MODELS.md has two entries with an unverified licence because the cache holds no model card for them; the models were still run, as the brief requires the models for the task.
openIssues: Whisper-small mis-hears synthetic voices (a German voice reading English gave nonsense; even the English voice is only tested on one sentence). The radio rule (WER at most 15 percent against the unfiltered transcript) will be noisy on synthesised lines.
CLAP margins on the current placeholder sounds are all negative; that is a statement about the placeholders, not a tool defect, but the neg list may be strict for the cabin loop.
The placeholder alarms have broadband clicks at the pulse onsets (seen in the spectrogram), which break the sensor and alarm rules.
forNextAgent: Run from the repo root with .venv-audio/Scripts/python.exe. measure.analyse(data, sr, loop) in tools/audio/listen/measure.py returns a plain dict (keys samplePeakDb, truePeakDb, clippedSamples, dcOffset, lufs, bands, lowShare, highShare, fundamentalHz, envelope{onsetMs, attackMs, fall60Ms, lastTenMsDb, printed}, loop{seamRatio, pass}); import it by adding tools/audio/listen to sys.path. compare.Clap().score(mono, sr, texts) and compare.judge(...) give CLAP numbers; transcribe.wer(ref, hyp) and transcribe.Whisper().transcribe(...) for speech; describe.Describer().ask(mono, sr, question) for Qwen (exit code 3 from the CLI if it cannot load). All model use must sit inside common.gpu_lock(label). Pitfalls: this machine's default Windows speech voice is German (select an en-* voice for English tests); the bash tool in this environment failed on long heredocs, so write files with the Write tool; 0 dBFS-clipped threshold is 0.9999; loop checks are only for loops; the batch compare result goes to assets/audio/cache/compare.json unless --out is given.
